PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
This is the portion of the meeting set aside for general public comment directly related to City business, for matters that do
not appear on this evening’s agenda. If you are here for a specific agenda item that is under Unfinished Business or New 
Business, please wait until we reach that item. Items under First Reading & Referral will be discussed when they return 
under Unfinished Business, and we will hear public comment at that time. Public comment requires a person to state your 
name and whether you are a resident of Bangor. The City Council has adopted a Public Comment Policy that we will 
adhere to. Statements during public comment should respect the dignity and seriousness of the proceeding, and individuals 
will be restricted to speaking once. Obscene, truly threatening, or overly repetitive comments will be deemed out of order 
and will be interrupted and removed. Topics that are considered out of order also include matters that are in litigation, 
individual employees or employee groups discussing matters for which complaint or grievance procedures are in place, 
personal disputes between the speaker and another resident not germane to City business, support for or opposition to any 
candidate for political office, and personnel complaints pertaining to individual City employees. There is a time limit of 
three minutes per speaker, and the total time allowed for general public comment regarding City business will be limited to 
no more than one hour. The public comment period is for City Council members to listen and not to respond or debate 
with persons. If you do not live in Bangor or own property in Bangor, please allow those who do to have the opportunity to 
speak first. If you’d like to offer comment on any item directly related to City business not appearing on the regular 
agenda, you may approach the podium. Alternatively, Councilors may be reached via email 
at councilors@bangormaine.gov. (A link to the adopted public comment policy can be found on the City’s website.)

Executive Summary: This Resolve will authorize the acceptance and appropriation of $2,638,248.72. The 
funds will be used for bathroom upgrades for ADA compliance and skylight replacement at the Bangor 
International Airport domestic terminal.
A PFC is a charge paid by passengers that is used to make improvements to the Airport's infrastructure that 
benefits the passengers.  The current charge is $4.50 per passenger and is collected by the airlines when a 
ticket is purchased.  The airlines are able to deduct a small administrative fee of $0.11 and remit the 
balance of $4.39 to the Airport.
The FAA requested that the Airport submit a new PFC application for restroom upgrades and skylight 
replacement. The bathrooms will need to be upgraded to meet ADA compliance and the skylight replaced 
to protect the checkpoint upgrades. 
A new PFC application needs to be filed in the amount of $2,638,248.72 to pay for the design, 
construction, and construction administration of these features of the project. These funds will supplement 
the initial PFC application (PFC Application #7) to complete this project.

Development Committee meeting.

Amendment to the KRT Appraisal Contract for the 
Property Equalization Project (Revaulation)
HAWES
Executive Summary: This Order, if passed, would allow the City Manager to execute an amendment to 
the 2024 KRT Appraisal Contract for the Property Equalization Project (Revaluation).
KRT Appraisal was required to deliver all final project deliverables and complete the revaluation project 
no later than July 24, 2026. Once it became obvious to the City and KRT Appraisal that this deadline 
would not be met, the City and KRT Appraisal entered into negotiations to (1) amend the deadline date 
contained in the 2024 KRT Appraisal Contract, and (2) determine the amount of liquidated damages KRT 
Appraisal will pay to the City.
The amendment will require that KRT Appraisal provide the final deliverables and completed revaluation 
project no later than April 19, 2027, with interim deliverables outlined in the amendment, and total net 
retainage of $60,000 for agreed-upon liquidated damages.

City Councilors Present: Fish, Mallar, Carson, Faloon, Walker, Deane, Hawes,

City Staff Present: Krieg, Robbins, Saavedra 
 
Chair Leonard called the meeting to order at 5:57 P.M.  
 
 
1. Holiday Banners – Downtown Bangor Partnership  
 
Chair Leonard introduced the agenda item. 
 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg presented on the proposed new 
downtown decorations. 
 
Councilor Deane asked if they are the same size as previous ban ners – Community and 
Economic Development Director Krieg responded they are the same size. 
 
Councilor Mallar asked what the magic wand installment is. Moni que Bouchard, 
Downtown Bangor Partnership staff, responded that it is a proje ct where retailers and 
storefront owners have a transponder that is triggered by a “ma gic wand” to impact the 
lights, and discussed a collaboration with the Bangor Public Li brary. Councilor Beck 
provided positive feedback on the proposed project. 
 
Councilor Beck asked if the photo display with the tree last ye ar is returning -- Monique 
Bouchard confirmed and discussed the expanded opportunity for photo displays this year.  
 
Councilor Deane asked if there would be a connection to the renovated Pickering Square 
area or the waterfront – Monique Bouchard responded that it is contingent upon 
completion of electrical components in the area. Chair Leonard noted that it is difficult to 
find the outlets for access. Councilor Fish complimented how Pickering Square looks. 
 
Chair Leonard asked who designed the banners – Monique Bouchard responded she did. 
Leonard noted that the artist community is against use of AI in  art and that he does not 
endorse its use. Bouchard responded that they were all done by her and that they have a 
commitment to creating art in-house or by working with designers.  
 
Councilor Faloon thanked the Downtown Bangor Partnership for their work around holiday 
decorations. 
 
Councilor Carson moved that the Committee approve the banners. Seconded by 
Councilor Faloon. Vote unless doubted, no doubt.
2. Customer Facility Charge (CFC ) Appropriation – Bangor Intern ational 
Airport 
 
Chair Leonard introduced the agenda item. 
 
Assistant Airport Director Robbins presented on the customer facility charge (CFC) for car 
rentals to improve and expand facilities that car rental custom ers use and the proposed 
appropriation to begin designing a consolidated rental car faci lity to meet current needs 
and leave room for growth.  
 
Chair Leonard asked whether it may be covering the same respons ibilities as past 
conversations. Assistant Airport Director Robbins responded and  referenced the Master 
Plan, using this appropriation to proceed to the next steps. Le onard discussed concerns 
surrounding knowing what sites to work with and moving forward with a consultant plan. 
 
Councilor Carson expressed excitement about this in alignment w ith record growth and 
the exploration of airline expansion.  
 
Assistant Airport Director Robbins noted that questions can be prepared for Airport 
Director Saavedra. 
 
Councilor Fish expressed support for bringing the conversation around separating the 
rental facility and keeping it close to maintain a relationship  forward into a concept and 
next steps. 
 
Councilor Mallar expressed concern around not going to bid for this project and it being 
included in the five-year comprehensive bidding. Airport Director Saavedra responded that 
the airport solicits engineering services for five-year periods  that include comprehensive 
engineering services. Mallar asked if it would be redundant to approve this component 
again. Saavedra responded that the current request for approval  is not the contract, but 
rather the appropriation of the CFC funds that have been collected.  
 
Chair Leonard asked how necessary it is to move forward with th is appropriation to 
continue with the facilitation of the airport’s plan and noted wanting to service taxpayers 
more so than partners at the airport. Airport Director Saavedra  responded that the CFC 
funds are paid by airport users, rather than taxpayer dollars. Saavedra discussed that 
upgrades to facilities for car rental companies is a dire need to be addressed. Assistant 
Airport Director Robbins discussed that upon the appropriation,  they are granted nine 
months of planning, so if the appropriation is postponed until budget season, it will create 
further delay. 
 
Councilor Mallar asked about the terms of Mead & Hunt’s contrac t – Assistant Airport 
Director Robbins responded they were selected in 2025 to be the  engineer of record and 
it is for a five-year period. Mallar asked if the contract is open-ended as far as dollar value 
– Robbins confirmed. Robbins added that it is balanced on the F AA side with an 
independent fee estimate to evaluate reasonable rates.  
 
Councilor Fish moved to recommend to full Council the appropria tion of $222,040. 
Seconded by Councilor Carson. Vote unless doubted, no doubt.

MEETING MINUTES 
 
City Councilors Present: Cote, Dinkins, Beck, Hawes, Pratt, Carson, Mallar (via 
Zoom) 
 
City Staff Present: Krieg, Saavedra, Innis 
 
Chair Hawes called the meeting to order at 6:19 P.M.  
 
 
1. Department Staff, Service and Program Overview  
 
Chair Hawes introduced the agenda item. 
 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg introduced he rself and provided 
an overview of the Community and Economic Development Departmen t and each 
imbedded division. She discussed opportunities to share informa tion about the varying 
projects the department works on.   
 
 
2. PFC Application and Revised Temporary Lease – Bangor Interna tional 
Airport 
 
Chair Hawes introduced the agenda item. 
 
Airport Director Saavedra discussed updates with the PFC Applic ation surrounding 
restroom updates and skylight replacement. 
 
Chair Hawes asked the Committee for questions – Councilor Beck clarified how the items 
should be voted on.  
 
Councilor Beck moved to approve airport staff to submit the PFC  Application #8 in the 
amount of $2,403,510.02. Seconded by Councilor Dinkins. Roll ca ll vote conducted – all 
in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.  
 
Councilor Beck moved to allow airport staff to accept and appro priate the $2,403,510.02 
if it is received from their PFC Application #8. Seconded by Councilor Cote. Roll call vote 
conducted – all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Airport Director Saavedra discussed a requested adjustment to a temporary lease. 
 
Councilor Beck moved to approve the change to the lease for GE Vernova. Seconded by 
Councilor Cote. Roll call vote conducted – all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
 
3. Commission on Cultural Development – Fall 2026 Grant Awards
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg discussed that the Commission on 
Cultural Development unanimously voted to recommend awarding fi ve grants for a total 
of $20,000 to five organizations. She provided background on the Commission on Cultural 
Development, including the grant cycle, ARTober, and the Arts & Culture Strategy Plan.  
 
Councilor Mallar asked whether the Form 990 is asked for to mak e sure they are current 
– Commissioner Snow, Commission on Cultural Development Grant Subcommittee Chair, 
responded that it is not something currently asked for as part of the application process. 
Mallar requested a Form 990 be asked for to ensure organization s are a valid nonprofit. 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg responded tha t they will include 
that in the application moving forward. 
 
Councilor Dinkins asked if the grant program that has been done every year – Community 
and Economic Development Director Krieg responded she believes it has been done for 
ten years. 
 
Councilor Beck asked how many applicants the grants received – Commissioner Snow 
responded five.  
 
Councilor Beck discussed how the $20,000 is an investment in the City with the attraction 
to various productions and asked if there is an estimate of how that trickles into economic 
development. Commissioner Snow discussed that the Downtown Bangor Partnership had 
completed a study examining what someone visiting town for a production or show spends 
in the area. 
 
Councilor Cote asked if Some Theatre Company is currently locat ed in the mall – 
Commissioner Snow responded that they were in the mall, but hav e secured rehearsal 
space at the Morgan Hill Event Center and performance space at the old Bangor Arts 
Exchange location, so they are still planning on their December  performance of Les 
Misérables. 
 
Councilor Beck moved that the Committee recommends approval of the applications as 
detailed in the memo. Seconded by Councilor Cote. Roll call vote conducted – all in favor, 
none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
 
4. Executive Session: Consultations with legal counsel 1 M.R.S.A. § 405(6)(E) – 1 
item & Acquisition of real property or economic development 1 M.R.S.A. § 405(6)(C) 
– 2 items 
  
Councilor Beck moved to enter executive session pursuant to 1 M .R.S.A. § 405(6)(E), 
consultations with legal counsel, and 1 M.R.S.A. § 405(6)(C), a cquisition of real property 
or economic development. Seconded by Councilor Cote. Roll call vote conducted – all in 
favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
 
4. Possible Actions on Executive Session Item 
 
Council Chair Carson noted that Committee Chair Hawes had to st ep away and the 
Committee needs to nominate a chair to finish business.  
 
Councilor Cote nominated Councilor Beck. Seconded by Councilor Dinkins. Councilor 
Beck accepted.
Acting Chair Beck noted he will entertain motions on potential actions based on executive 
session. Acting City Solicitor Innis provided reminders on how to proceed with motions.  
 
Councilor Dinkins moved to authorize the extension of three yea rs for the contract 
between Irving Oil and the City of Bangor. Seconded by Councilo r Cote. Roll call vote 
conducted – all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed and item forwarded to full Council. 
 
Councilor Cote moved to move forward with the Tax Increment Financing (TIF) and Credit 
Enhancement Agreement (CEA) application for the Milford Street Extension. Seconded 
by Councilor Dinkins.  
 
Councilor Mallar asked what the cost is going to be of an outsi de attorney for the TIF 
application – Community and Economic Development Director Krieg responded they can 
get an estimate. Mallar discussed that he would like to know wh at the expense will be 
regardless if the application goes through.  
 
Councilor Cote rescinded his motion. Councilor Dinkins rescinde d his second. Acting 
Chair Beck noted there will be further discussion once staff provides more information. 
  
Councilor Dinkins moved to recommend that two parcels, R55-004-B and R61-021-C, are 
sold back to A&L Webster LLC. Seconded by Councilor Cote. Roll call vote conducted – 
two in favor (Beck, Dinkins), two opposed (Mallar, Cote). Motion failed.

Accepting and Appropriating Passenger Facility Charge #8 funds in the amount of $2,638,248.72 for Terminal 
Bathroom Upgrades and Skylight Replacement
This Resolve will authorize the acceptance and appropriation of $2,638,248.72. The funds will be 
used for bathroom upgrades for ADA compliance and skylight replacement at the Bangor 
International Airport domestic terminal. 
 
A PFC is a charge paid by passengers that is used to make improvements to the Airport's 
infrastructure that benefits the passengers.  The current charge is $4.50 per passenger and is 
collected by the airlines when a ticket is purchased.  The airlines are able to deduct a small 
administrative fee of $0.11 and remit the balance of $4.39 to the Airport. 
 
The FAA requested that the Airport submit a new PFC application for restroom upgrades and skylight 
replacement. The bathrooms will need to be upgraded to meet ADA compliance and the skylight 
replaced to protect the checkpoint upgrades.  
 
A new PFC application needs to be filed in the amount of $2,638,248.72 to pay for the design, 
construction, and construction administration of these features of the project. These funds will 
supplement the initial PFC application (PFC Application #7) to complete this project. 
 
This item was reviewed and recommended for approval at the November 16, 2026 Business & 
Economic Development Committee meeting.

schedule and assess liquidated damages in the amount of $60,000 against KRT Appraisal due to the delay;

Equalization Project (Revaluation) which will incorporate a revised project timeline culminating an effective 
valuation date of April 1, 2027 and total net retainage for agreed-upon liquidated damages in the amount of 
$60,000. The final form of the amendment shall be approved by the City's Legal Department.
